h: Wyre Forest Wanders and Stourport's Canal Basins
p: West Midlands Safari Park is a big day out, so a bit of planning helps you get the most from it. Arrive early to beat the queues, and plan your day around your timed safari slot, as missing it would be a real shame. Fill up the car before you arrive, keep snacks and drinks within reach for the drive-through, and make sure any phones or cameras are charged for those close-up moments with the animals.

Once you're on foot, grab a map and pick your must-sees, as the walk-round area and rides can easily take up the whole afternoon. A change of clothes might come in handy if any water rides are open, and comfy shoes are essential.

Bewdley sits right on the edge of the Wyre Forest, a sprawling ancient woodland that's perfect for walks, cycle rides and wildlife-spotting. The Wyre Forest Visitor Centre near Callow Hill is a good starting point, with waymarked trails, a café and play areas.

Down in town, Bewdley Museum tells the story of the area's crafts and trades, from rope-making to clay pipes, in the old butchers' shambles. For a change of scene, head downriver to Stourport-on-Severn, a Georgian canal town where the Staffordshire and Worcestershire Canal meets the River Severn. Its canal basins are lovely to stroll around, with narrowboats tied up beside handsome old warehouses, and the riverside meadows are made for an ice cream. It's a great way to wind down after the excitement of the safari.
